Hi Sarah / Neha — quick technical note ahead of the call. I profiled a representative LLM run from DataNova (seq len ~512, batch 8 in production traces) and found the following approximate service-level numbers on our standard runtime build: 

- A100 (baseline): p50 ~ 115 tokens/sec, p95 ~ 72 tokens/sec (single-stream, steady-state)
- H100: p50 ~ 210 tokens/sec, p95 ~ 140 tokens/sec
- L40S (dense, int8/quantized paths): p50 ~ 160 tokens/sec, p95 ~ 110 tokens/sec

Performance-per-dollar (rough, normalized to cost per hour):
- A100: baseline = 1.0 perf/$
- H100: ~1.7x perf/$ for inference-heavy workloads (models with large kv-cache where tensor-core speedups matter)
- L40S: ~1.3x perf/$ for high-throughput batched workloads where quantization is acceptable

Operational recommendation:
- Keep 8x reserved A100 for latency-sensitive baseline traffic and convert the additional 8x reserved to H100 if you want headroom for low-latency spikes and RLHF-style chat workloads. That gives the best p95 improvement for tail latency-sensitive requests.
- Alternatively, if most workloads are high-throughput batched embedding/rerank, consider L40S for the reserved increment and add a small H100 burst pool for low-latency paths.

Committed throughput guarantees we can reasonably offer on a reserved pool (with 99.5% uptime and our autoscaling config):
- For 8x H100 reserved pool: guaranteed baseline throughput ~ 8 * p95(H100) = 8 * 140 = ~1120 tokens/sec (aggregate), with documented fallbacks to compatible variants if unavailable.
- For 8x A100 reserved pool: guaranteed baseline throughput ~ 8 * 72 = ~576 tokens/sec (aggregate).

Caveats: exact numbers depend on model variant, sequence length distribution, and whether quantized execution is acceptable. I’ll prepare a short worksheet (Performance_per_Dollar_Worksheet.xlsx) that takes your real traces and outputs expected aggregate qps and monthly cost for each config.

Vivek
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
